headline: Cyberattack may have exposed Chase Bank and Mastercard customer data
author: Violet Jira

paragraphs.text: Cyberattackers may have accessed the names and email addresses of some JPMorgan Chase and Mastercard customers, the financial giants said Thursday. Visa in a statement also said it was aware of claims that its customers’ data had been affected, but it did not confirm any exposure.

Chase, Mastercard and Visa said that their own systems were not impacted. None of the companies have reported a disruption in service associated, and the companies said payment data, such as card numbers, was not affected.
All three companies said the incident involved a third-party service provider. None of the companies have named the vendor, and it is unclear whether the breaches were the result of the same attack.

The attacks arrived on the heels of incidents in which several other companies saw their systems affected by technological issues, though not cyberattacks in each instance. A global Microsoft outage disrupted access to Outlook and Microsoft 365 last week, and a nationwide ground stop by the Federal Aviation Administration was attributed to a telecommunications failure.

But those and a string of other disruptions in recent weeks — some of which have been linked to artificial intelligence — have put customers on edge and prompted institutions globally to take steps to brace themselves against cyberthreats.

Mastercard said in a statement Thursday that an incident at a third-party provider resulted in the exposure of a “limited amount of email addresses” of a small subset of customers enrolled in a specific program.

Chase said in a statement on X that a breach affecting third parties that work for the firm may have allowed attackers to access marketing data held by the vendors, which may have included names and emails.
Chase declined to comment further on who the vendors are, when the company became aware of the attack and how many customers’ data had been accessed.
Mastercard said that “the exposure has been contained” and that the company was working to support affected cardholders. Chase said affected customers would be contacted directly.

On Tuesday, Chase customers across the country couldn’t access some online banking services after a disruption in service that the company said was caused by “a software bug in on-premise hardware systems” and not a cyberattack. Service was restored Tuesday. That incident and the one Chase reported Thursday are unrelated, according to the company.
